newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia SBI index surges on new investment rules.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia SBI index surges on new investment rules.

text.p: Slovenian shares surged seven percent in early trade on Wednesday and traders said the index could gain at least another one percent by the end of the day due to relaxed rules for international investors.

"Everyone is buying. I do not know whether foreign investors are back as yet or whether domestic traders are buying in order to sell to foreigners later," said Goran Brankovic, a trader of bank Nova Ljubljanska Banka.

He said international investors were expected to come back en masse following a Bank of Slovenia decision to enable foreigners to invest without incurring extra bank charges provided they hold onto a share for at least seven years or trade among themselves.
Traders said as a consequence the index could rise to a record high of about 1,800 points by the end of August.

"This growth could only be stopped if Slovenia fails to ratify the association agreement with the European Union or if the central bank again limits foreign buying, but both things are unlikely to happen," one said.
The ratification of the accord, which was signed in June last year and is a precondition for EU membership, is expected by the end of July.
By 0940 GMT the blue-chip SBI index was up 7.05 percent or 94.52 points at 1,435.11.
Petrol trader Petrol was most active, up 8.43 percent to 20,580 on volume of 5,287 shares.
Analysts said Petrol, drug firms Lek and Krka and food maker Kolinska were expected to attract most foreign interest.
By 0940 GMT Lek was up 8.7 percent to 29,020 and Krka 9.6 percent to 21,800. Kolinska jumped 5.76 percent to 2,221.
